title: Who frees it?
description:
Make memory cross a DLL boundary safely by giving each side its own allocate and free.

```
lib_create_buffer(64) -> handle 1
host frees it with lib_free -> ok
host tries to free with its own free -> refused: allocated by the library
leak check: 0 live buffers
```
hints: Each side may use a different C runtime with its own heap; that is why the library must free what it allocated (lesson 2.05).

The library can allocate with `new unsigned char[size]` and free with `delete[] static_cast<unsigned char*>(p)`, remembering each block's size in `live` (`std::malloc` and `std::free` from `<cstdlib>` are the C-style way to do the same).
The host's own free can check `lib::live.count(p)` here; in real code you only find out when it crashes.
requirements: The "library" hands out buffers it allocates, and exports `lib_free`.
Track who allocated each block; freeing with the wrong function is reported.
At the end, report any blocks still alive.
stretch: Let the caller pass in an allocator (a pair of function pointers), as many C libraries allow.
